title: Teriyaki Chicken
subtitle: Japanese glazed chicken in a sweet soy sauce
excerpt: Chicken thighs grilled or pan-fried and glazed in a shiny, sweet-salty teriyaki sauce of soy, mirin, and sake. A Japanese classic, quick enough for a weeknight.

recipe.sourceNotes: Teriyaki (teri meaning gloss or sheen and yaki meaning grilled) is a Japanese cooking technique in which food is grilled or broiled while being basted with a sweet soy-based sauce that creates a characteristic glossy caramelised glaze. The technique dates back to at least the seventeenth century in Japan. Traditional teriyaki sauce is a simple combination of soy sauce, mirin (sweet rice wine), and sake, cooked together until the alcohol has evaporated and the sugars concentrate. Chicken thighs are the most common cut for home cooking because the higher fat content prevents them from drying out during the high-heat cooking required to caramelise the glaze. The teriyaki method can be applied to other proteins: salmon, beef, and tofu all work well with the same sauce.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy frying pan or griddle pan.

content.text: Score the chicken thighs through the skin in a few places before cooking: this helps the skin crisp and allows the glaze to penetrate. Start the chicken skin-side down in a cold pan before turning up the heat, which renders the fat from the skin slowly rather than burning the surface. The teriyaki sauce should reduce to a glossy, sticky consistency before the chicken is returned to it. Spoon the sauce over the chicken repeatedly as it finishes cooking to build up the glaze.

items.preparation: bone-in, skin-on; scored through the skin

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs skin-side down. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the skin is deeply golden and crisp. Turn and cook for 5 minutes more. Remove the chicken and set aside. Pour away excess fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon.

Pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan and bubble vigorously for 2 minutes until thick and glossy. Return the chicken to the pan and spoon the sauce over it. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, turning and basting, until the chicken is cooked through and coated in the glaze. Serve over rice scattered with spring onion and sesame seeds.
